# Class 3 {.ct}

![](../graphics/REB_Logo.png){fig-alt="Reaction Engineering Basics Logo" fig-align="center" width="200"}

## Rates and Rate Expressions {.cc}

Class 3 describes and defines reaction rates and empirical, theoretical, and mechanistic rate expressions. Rate coefficients and Arrhenius temperature dependence are introduced and explained.

## Learning Outcomes {.ch}

After completing Class 3 you should...

* Know
    * the definition of net rate, forward rate, reverse rate, reaction mechanism, empirical, theoretical, and mechanistic rate expressions, pre-exponential factor, activation energy, and typical, auto-catalytic, product-inhibited, and reactant-inhibited reactions
    * the defining equations for reaction rate, species generation rate, the Arrhenius expression, instantaneous yield, and instantaneous selectivity
* Understand
    * the functional form of rate expressions is only known a priori for elementary reactions
    * rate expressions must be experimentally validated
    * rate expressions must be single-valued and evaluate to zero at equilibrium
* Be able to
    * renormalize a reaction rate
    * convert reaction rates to species generation rates and vice versa
    * write a power-law rate expression
    * modify a rate expression so that the rate it predicts goes to zero as equilibrium is approached
    * estimate Arrhenius expression parameters using experimental data
    * assess whether a quantity displays Arrhenius temperature dependence given either data or an expression for its dependence on temperature
